title: Non-blocking finding from PR #345's review (frontend-ibkr-login-button-followups-followups)
description: Tracked follow-up for a non-blocking finding raised in pr-reviewer's review of PR #345 (frontend-ibkr-login-button-followups-followups) -- does not block the accept (a narrow-probability timing gap in an already-documented, bounded-severity heuristic, not a correctness regression, test/coverage drop, or methodology/architecture violation), but worth fixing so it isn't lost once PR #345 merges and the review comment disappears from view.

checklist.step: In `IbkrStatusIndicator.tsx`'s login button `onClick` handler, the `window.addEventListener('blur', handleBlurAfterClick)` call is registered AFTER `window.open(login_url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` returns, not before. If a browser/environment ever moves focus to the newly opened tab synchronously as part of processing `window.open()` (rather than deferring it to a later task/microtask) -- plausible in fast or automation-driven browser contexts, the same general class of timing sensitivity that caused the prior `document.hasFocus()`-after-300ms heuristic to misfire per this task's own dependency's checklist item 1 -- the `blur` event could fire and be gone before the listener is registered one line later. `focusLeftSinceClickRef.current` would never get set, so the 300ms cooldown timeout would incorrectly conclude the open was popup-blocked and clear `awaitingLoginReturnRef` even though a real login tab is open -- the next window-focus event (the user genuinely returning from a successful login) would then fail to trigger the intended immediate status refetch, silently falling back to the existing up-to-30s background poll (never a stuck-forever gate -- same bounded failure mode already accepted elsewhere in this component). Fix: move the `window.addEventListener('blur', handleBlurAfterClick)` call (and the `pendingBlurListenerRef.current = handleBlurAfterClick` assignment) to immediately before the `window.open(...)` call, closing this narrow window at no cost (per the code-review pass that raised this during PR #345's review).
